From 9d724b34fbe13b71865ad0906a4be97571f19cf5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kevin Hao <haokexin@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 10:47:03 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: cpsw_new: Fix potential unregister of netdev that has
 not been registered yet

If an error occurs during register_netdev() for the first MAC in
cpsw_register_ports(), even though cpsw->slaves[0].ndev is set to NULL,
cpsw->slaves[1].ndev would remain unchanged. This could later cause
cpsw_unregister_ports() to attempt unregistering the second MAC.
To address this, add a check for ndev->reg_state before calling
unregister_netdev(). With this change, setting cpsw->slaves[i].ndev
to NULL becomes unnecessary and can be removed accordingly.

Fixes: ed3525eda4c4 ("net: ethernet: ti: introduce cpsw switchdev based driver part 1 - dual-emac")
Signed-off-by: Kevin Hao <haokexin@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Alexander Sverdlin <alexander.sverdlin@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260205-cpsw-error-path-v1-2-6e58bae6b299@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c
index b9fc31eb0613..7f42f58a4b03 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c
@@ -1472,7 +1472,7 @@ static void cpsw_unregister_ports(struct cpsw_common *cpsw)
 
 	for (i = 0; i < cpsw->data.slaves; i++) {
 		ndev = cpsw->slaves[i].ndev;
-		if (!ndev)
+		if (!ndev || ndev->reg_state != NETREG_REGISTERED)
 			continue;
 
 		priv = netdev_priv(ndev);
@@ -1494,7 +1494,6 @@ static int cpsw_register_ports(struct cpsw_common *cpsw)
 		if (ret) {
 			dev_err(cpsw->dev,
 				"cpsw: err registering net device%d\n", i);
-			cpsw->slaves[i].ndev = NULL;
 			break;
 		}
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Modifications in Each File

**File:** `drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c`

1. **`cpsw_unregister_ports()`:** Added a condition to skip net devices that have not yet been fully registered. The line:
   ```c
   if (!ndev || ndev->reg_state != NETREG_REGISTERED)
   ```
   now prevents calling `unregister_netdev()` on a `net_device` whose registration state is not `NETREG_REGISTERED`.

2. **`cpsw_register_ports()`:** Removed the line that set the slave’s `ndev` pointer to `NULL` when `register_netdev()` fails.
   ```c
   cpsw->slaves[i].ndev = NULL;   // removed
   ```

## Relationship Between Modifications

The two changes are complementary and logically connected. When a net device fails to register, its `reg_state` field will not be `NETREG_REGISTERED`. The new check in `cpsw_unregister_ports()` therefore already protects against attempting to unregister such a device, making the explicit `ndev = NULL` assignment redundant. Removing that assignment simplifies the code and eliminates a potential source of inconsistency (e.g., forgetting to set `ndev = NULL` for other slaves in an error path). Together, these modifications correctly handle the error scenario where `register_netdev()` fails for one port while other ports remain partially initialized, preventing a later crash or double-free in the cleanup routine.
